diff_source: gh pr diff 574 → diff.patch (464 lines, 15 files, single chunk — under 3000-line threshold)

findings.title: Committed landlord-facing checklist PDF (priv/static/templates/tenant-vetting-checklist.pdf) still carries the pre-sweep sentence — the .typ was amended but the served artifact was never regenerated
findings.evidence: pdftotext of the committed PDF at the reviewed sha: 'Their track record / Ask for references from the current and previous landlord, and an employer. Then actually contact them.' — the OLD sentence. git diff origin/develop...HEAD --stat touches 15 files, no .pdf. No Makefile/CI/Dockerfile step regenerates it (Dockerfile installs typst only for runtime audit-report generation). Last regenerated in 2f2c186 alongside the original .typ.
findings.detail: Spec item 3 amends the landlord-facing vetting checklist; the HTML page got the new sentence but the downloadable PDF — the artifact landlords actually save/print — still reads 'and an employer.' pdftotext confirms. Found while verifying tests[1].
findings.recommended_fix: Regenerate the PDF from the amended tenant-vetting-checklist.typ (typst compile) and commit the binary; verify pdftotext shows the scoped sentence.

findings.title: Changed upload_required_message copy has no text assertion — tests pin only the error keys
findings.evidence: validate_files_presence tests assert e.0 == "employer_ref_primary" (application_handler_test.gleam:783) — key only. grep -rn "Upload an employer" server/test/ returns nothing.
findings.detail: Both ruled strings on the required-upload error path changed; a typo in the ruled copy ships green.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend the employer_ref branch of validate_files_presence_requires_* tests to assert e.1 equals the ruled strings (primary and co-applicant ordinal fallback).

findings.title: tenant-vetting-checklist.typ sentence change has zero test contact — template never compiled or content-asserted
findings.evidence: content_test.gleam:36,907,1567 import/render the checklist VIEW (HTML), never the .typ. The typst-CLI compile pattern exists only for audit_report.typ (audit_report_test.gleam:3-5, skip-locally/panic-in-CI). content_test.gleam:847 checklist_pdf_is_committed_test only asserts the committed PDF is readable bits.
findings.detail: A Typst syntax error or copy typo in the amended line passes make test green — and in fact the stale committed PDF (blocker above) shipped green for the same reason.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a compile check for tenant-vetting-checklist.typ mirroring audit_report_test's typst-CLI pattern, or a source-content assertion on the amended sentence; a content assertion on the committed PDF's provenance would have caught the stale artifact.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
findings.evidence: Component findings each independently confirmed: P0 form paths fully pinned; P1 partial (upload_required_message text, audit-PDF labels compile-only, co-applicant banner labels drift-only); two surfaces NONE (offline .typ, HTML checklist sentence) — overall just under the 80% PASS line.
findings.detail: P0 100%; P1 ~85%; overall ~78% (13/20 changed surfaces FULL, 5 PARTIAL, 2 NONE).
findings.recommended_fix: Raise to PASS by pinning upload_required_message text, asserting the amended sentence on the HTML checklist view, compile-checking tenant-vetting-checklist.typ, and extending error_summary text pins to the co-applicant employer-ref labels.

findings.title: Employer-ref count-cap rejection message on the same Documents step still uses the pre-sweep term "employer reference"
findings.evidence: document_upload.gleam:167: "One employer reference per adult \u2014 that\u2019s four at most." — surfaced to applicants via application_handler.gleam:1452 `document_upload.CountCapExceeded(message) -> [#("documents", message)]`, while the same PR renamed the sibling required-upload errors (application_handler.gleam:964,969).
findings.detail: Reachable via crafted multi-file posts (slots are single-file; precheck_uploads enforces server-side). Not in the PR's disclosed left-untouched list. Copy is user-ruled, so this needs a ruling, not a drive-by edit.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword to 'One employer / business reference per adult — that's four at most.' (user ruling) or add the surface to the disclosed deferred list.

findings.title: New validation test appends a duplicate num_occupants key; first-match-wins get_form_value keeps the base "1", so the constructed 2-adult household never exists
findings.evidence: test_helpers.gleam:141: #("num_occupants", "1") in valid_application_form_values(); the new test does list.append([#("num_occupants", "2"), ...]); get_form_value (application_handler.gleam:2274-2277) uses list.key_find — first match wins, the appended "2" is dead.
findings.detail: Assertions still pass (they target employer-trio messages, unaffected by occupancy), but the fixture is internally inconsistent: num_occupants=1 alongside co_applicant_count=1.
findings.recommended_fix: Replace list.append for num_occupants with list.key_set("num_occupants", "2").

findings.title: Only employer_name gets the business-aware label; other employer-trio fact keys (employer_letter_signatory) keep employer-only labels
findings.evidence: evidence_humanize.gleam:215-216 allowlists employer_name and employer_letter_signatory; display_label_for_key special-cases only employer_name; the unchanged test still expects "Employer letter signatory: Niall Foley".
findings.detail: Spec item 2 scopes the unify to the employer_name data line ('one field, one label'), so this looks deliberate — but the signatory label also assumes an employer for a sole trader. Worth a conscious confirm, not a change.
findings.recommended_fix: Confirm scope is deliberate; otherwise extend display_label_for_key to the remaining employer-trio fact keys.

findings.title: display_label_for_key doc comment claims stored analyses both keep the old label and self-heal
findings.evidence: "analyses stored before the ruling keep the old label on re-render — cosmetic, historical-only, self-healing."
findings.detail: A stored analysis that keeps the old label on re-render never heals; what heals is the surface population as new analyses land. Minor internal-comment tension.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword: historical analyses keep the old label permanently; only new analyses get the new label.

findings.title: Four-item applicant checklist duplicated verbatim across email_client and form_view; second consecutive sweep PR required to edit both
findings.evidence: email_client.gleam:264,267 vs form_view.gleam:149,152 — identical item strings ("A name, phone number and email address for each referee.", "About 15 minutes, once you have the documents.") as independent literals in two modules.
findings.detail: #573 and #574 both had to edit the identical sentence in both places; a future ruling can silently land on only one surface. Hoisting is follow-up refactor, not this PR's scope.
findings.recommended_fix: Hoist the four item strings into server/src/copy.gleam (checklist_items() -> List(String)); have requirements_checklist_html and view_prep_block render from it.

findings.title: Stale 'Employer reference' doc comments in document_upload.gleam after sibling module doc was updated to the new label
findings.evidence: 103: "/// Employer reference: one per adult (primary + up to three co-applicants)," and 346: "/// Employer reference document — one per adult (primary + co-applicants)," — while the PR updated the analogous doc in form_sections/documents.gleam.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword both doc comments to 'Employer / business reference' to match the documents.gleam module doc updated in this PR.

findings.title: HTML vetting-checklist sentence change unasserted — the view is rendered in tests only for og/tracking checks
findings.evidence: grep -rn "Ask for references" server/test/ returns nothing; content_test.gleam:1567-1601 renders the page but asserts only posthog/fbq/gtag init snippets.
findings.detail: Sibling surfaces (invite email, prep block) got pins; this one didn't.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a string.contains assertion for the amended track-record sentence to content_test.gleam against tenant_vetting_checklist_view.render.

findings.title: Audit PDF 'Employer / business reference' labels covered at compile level only — no rendered-text assertion
findings.evidence: audit_report_test.gleam:218-220 asserts byte_size != 0 and <<"%PDF-":utf8>> magic only; maximal_snapshot() exercises both changed hunks, so template breakage fails but a label typo would compile green.
findings.detail: PDF text extraction is impractical at unit level; compile-level coverage is a defensible floor.
findings.recommended_fix: Accept compile-level coverage, or add a lightweight source-grep test asserting audit_report.typ contains 'Employer / business reference' and not the old standalone label.

findings.title: Co-applicant 'employer / business reference document' banner labels unpinned — only the non-fallback drift test touches those keys
findings.evidence: error_summary_test.gleam:100-102 lists employer_ref_coapplicant_0/1/2 only in curated_keys_with_compound_labels (asserts curated != humanise(key)); label_for_mapped_keys_test pins only employer_ref_primary.
findings.detail: A typo in one co-applicant variant stays green.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend label_for_mapped_keys_test (or a small table test) to assert the exact ruled text for employer_ref_coapplicant_0/1/2.

rejected_findings.title: Test asserts label_for("employer_name") == "Employer / business name" but this diff never changes that mapping
rejected_findings.reason: False positive from diff-only view: the mapping IS present at error_summary.gleam:151 in the worktree — it landed via #573 (e7bab72), which is in this branch's history (rebased onto develop post-#573). CI runs against the rebased tree; the test passes.

rejected_findings.title: "if you're working" fails to route self-employed applicants
rejected_findings.reason: Binding round context: ALL copy in this PR is verbatim user ruling — wording flags are out of bounds. Also factually wrong: the sentence's second clause ('or from a client, accountant, or business contact if you're self-employed') is exactly the sole-trader route.

rejected_findings.title: Test comment reads 'the daft auto-reply' — likely a typo for 'draft'
rejected_findings.reason: False positive from missing domain context: 'daft auto-reply' is the auto-reply to daft.ie listing leads — email_parser.gleam:146 matches @daft.ie; the PR body uses the same term deliberately.
